question: What breaks my focus on a spell?
gold key facts: Another concentration spell; damage (Con save, DC 10 or half the damage); incapacitated or killed; GM-called DC 10 save for environmental effects; you can end it at will; normal activity is fine.

question: Do I need to see a target to attack it?
gold key facts: No. You can attack a target you cannot see, but with disadvantage; if it is not where you aimed, the attack misses.

question: Can I punish an unseen enemy that runs away from me?
gold key facts: No. An opportunity attack needs a hostile creature that you can see moving out of your reach.

question: Can I cast a spell while a silence effect is on me?
gold key facts: Not a spell with a verbal component. Spells without V can still be cast.

question: Can I shove a creature much bigger than me?
gold key facts: No. The target of a shove must be no more than one size larger than you.

question: How many magic items can one creature bond with?
gold key facts: Three at a time; a fourth attunement fails until you end one; no two copies of the same item.

question: Can I rest twice in a single day to recover everything?
gold key facts: No. A character cannot benefit from more than one long rest in a 24-hour period.

question: Can a creature that is held by an enemy still walk away?
gold key facts: No. A grappled creature's speed becomes 0 (it can try to escape the grapple instead).

question: Does teleporting away from an enemy provoke an attack?
gold key facts: No. Teleporting does not provoke an opportunity attack.

question: Can a surprised character act in the first round?
gold key facts: No. A surprised creature cannot move or take an action on its first turn and cannot take a reaction until that turn ends.

question: What happens if a character plunges off a cliff?
gold key facts: 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 10 feet fallen, maximum 20d6, and you land prone.

question: When does a character die outright instead of falling unconscious?
gold key facts: When damage takes you to 0 HP and the remaining damage is at least your hit point maximum (massive damage).

question: Can I cast a second leveled spell after a bonus action spell?
gold key facts: No. After casting a spell with a bonus action you can only cast a cantrip with a casting time of 1 action that turn.

question: Can I concentrate on two spells at once?
gold key facts: No. You cannot concentrate on two spells at once.

question: Can I recover from exhaustion by resting?
gold key facts: Yes. Finishing a long rest reduces exhaustion by 1 (with some food and drink).

question: How long can a creature hold its breath?
gold key facts: 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds).

question: Can two clerics cast the same blessing on one ally to stack it?
gold key facts: No. The same spell cast several times does not combine; the most potent effect applies.

question: Can I disengage and still be hit as I leave?
gold key facts: No. Taking the Disengage action means your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

question: Can I take two reactions before my next turn?
gold key facts: No. You cannot take another reaction until the start of your next turn.

question: Is a paralyzed creature able to act?
gold key facts: No. Paralyzed means incapacitated and unable to move or speak.

question: Can I double my proficiency bonus twice on the same roll?
gold key facts: No. Your proficiency bonus cannot be added to a single roll more than once.

question: Can advantage and disadvantage cancel each other out?
gold key facts: Yes. If you have both, they cancel and you roll one d20, however many sources of each there are.

question: Can the Dash action be used as a bonus action?
gold key facts: Only through a specific feature, such as the rogue's Cunning Action; otherwise Dash is an action.

question: Can a prone creature stand up for free?
gold key facts: No. Standing up costs movement equal to half your speed.

question: Can a monster use a legendary action in the middle of its own turn?
gold key facts: No. Legendary actions are used only at the end of another creature's turn, one at a time.
